target: Akad nikah dimulai jam sembilan pagi, resepsinya sore hari.
english: The vow ceremony starts at nine in the morning; the reception is in the afternoon.
tip: Akad (nikah) = the short vow ceremony; the resepsi is the big party afterwards.

target: Banyak tamu memakai batik ke resepsi pernikahan itu.
english: Many guests wore batik to that wedding reception.
tip: Batik is wedding wear: a good batik shirt is always right at a resepsi.

target: Lamaran mereka berjalan lancar minggu lalu di rumah calon mertua.
english: Their proposal went smoothly last week at the future in-laws' house.
tip: Calon = future/-to-be: calon mertua = future in-laws, calon suami = husband-to-be.

target: Amplopnya ditaruh di kotak dekat pintu masuk gedung.
english: The envelope is placed in a box near the hall entrance.
tip: Wedding guests give cash in an amplop (envelope), dropped in a box at the door — not handed over.

target: Selamat menempuh hidup baru untuk kalian berdua!
english: Congratulations on your new life together, you two!
tip: Selamat menempuh hidup baru = the set wedding wish: 'safe journey into the new life'.

target: Setelah menikah, mereka tinggal sementara di rumah mertua.
english: After getting married, they are living at the in-laws' house for a while.
tip: Mertua = your spouse's parents; menantu = your child's spouse. Rumah mertua = the in-laws' house.

target: Hari ini ulang tahun ibu saya yang keenam puluh.
english: Today is my mother's sixtieth birthday.
tip: yang ke- + number = ordinal: ulang tahun yang keenam puluh = sixtieth birthday.

target: Selamat ulang tahun, semoga panjang umur dan sehat selalu!
english: Happy birthday — may you have a long life and always be healthy!
tip: Selamat + noun makes a wish: selamat ulang tahun, selamat jalan, selamat makan.

target: Kado apa yang cocok untuk anak umur lima tahun?
english: What present is right for a five-year-old child?
tip: Kado = a wrapped present (from Dutch cadeau); hadiah is the wider word for gift or prize.

target: Dia mentraktir kami makan bakso karena baru ulang tahun.
english: He treated us to meatball soup because he just had a birthday.
tip: Indonesian birthdays flip the treat: the birthday person mentraktir (treats) the friends.

target: Kami menginap tiga malam di rumah kakek waktu Lebaran.
english: We stayed three nights at grandpa's house during Lebaran.
tip: Lebaran = the Eid homecoming holiday, when the whole country travels to family.

target: Setiap mudik, jalan ke kampung selalu macet parah.
english: Every homecoming trip, the road to the village is always badly jammed.
tip: Mudik = the big trip home to your family town before Lebaran — half the country moves at once.

target: Kami mengobrol sampai tengah malam di teras rumah.
english: We chatted until midnight on the terrace of the house.
tip: Mengobrol = to chat; in speech you will hear it shortened to ngobrol everywhere.

target: Tante membuatkan kami teh manis hangat sore itu.
english: Auntie made us warm sweet tea that afternoon.
tip: Adding -kan aims the action at a beneficiary: membuat teh = made tea, membuatkan kami teh = made tea for us. The person served comes right after the verb.

target: Jangan lupa cium tangan kakek waktu datang dan pamit.
english: Don't forget to kiss grandpa's hand when you arrive and when you say goodbye.
tip: Cium tangan — a child presses the elder's hand to the face — is the greeting for grandparents.

target: Selamat atas kelahiran anak pertama kalian!
english: Congratulations on the birth of your first child!
tip: Selamat atas + noun congratulates: selamat atas kelahiran = congrats on the birth.

target: Semoga usaha baru kamu berjalan lancar, ya.
english: I hope your new business goes smoothly, okay?
tip: Semoga + clause = hopefully/may: semoga lancar = hope it goes smoothly.

target: Selamat hari raya, mohon maaf lahir dan batin.
english: Happy Eid — please forgive my wrongs, outward and inward.
tip: The Eid greeting: mohon maaf lahir dan batin = forgive my wrongs, outward and inward.

target: Selamat menikmati masa pensiun, Pak Hasan!
english: Enjoy your retirement, Mr. Hasan!
tip: Selamat + verb blesses an activity: selamat menikmati = enjoy, selamat belajar = happy studying.

target: Selamat jalan, hati-hati, kabari kami kalau sudah sampai.
english: Safe travels, take care — let us know when you've arrived.
tip: Kabar is the noun 'news'; the -i ending turns it into a verb: kabari kami = send us word. Indonesian builds verbs straight from nouns this way all the time.

target: Turut berduka cita, ya. Semoga keluarga diberi ketabahan.
english: My deepest condolences. May the family be given strength.
tip: Turut berduka cita = the set condolence, 'I share the grief'; the reply is a quiet terima kasih.

target: Jangan lupa bawa oleh-oleh kalau pulang dari Bali.
english: Don't forget to bring souvenirs when you come home from Bali.
tip: Oleh-oleh = treats you bring people after a trip — coming home empty-handed is not done.

target: Titip oleh-oleh dodol, ya, kalau kamu ke Garut.
english: Get me some dodol, okay, if you go to Garut.
tip: Titip = ask a traveler to get you something: titip dodol = bring me back some dodol.

target: Kado untuk pengantin sudah saya bungkus rapi tadi malam.
english: I already wrapped the present for the couple neatly last night.
tip: Object + sudah saya + bare verb = natural passive: sudah saya bungkus = I have wrapped it.

target: Selain kue, kami juga membawakan keponakan mainan.
english: Besides cakes, we also brought our nephews and nieces toys.
tip: membawakan puts the person right after the verb: membawakan keponakan mainan = brought the nieces and nephews toys.

target: Kita perlu menyiapkan kursi tambahan untuk para sepupu.
english: We need to prepare extra chairs for all the cousins.
tip: Para + person noun = plural group: para tamu = the guests, para sepupu = the cousins.

target: Rumah terasa sepi setelah semua saudara pulang ke kota masing-masing.
english: The house feels quiet after all the relatives went home to their own cities.
tip: Masing-masing sits after the noun and covers 'their own' by itself: kota masing-masing = their own cities – no separate word for 'their' needed.

target: Setelah tiga bulan les, saya akhirnya bisa berenang sampai ujung kolam.
english: After three months of lessons, I can finally swim to the end of the pool.
tip: Bisa = ability: bisa berenang = can swim. For permission Indonesian uses boleh, not bisa.

target: Saya sudah bisa menyetir, tapi belum boleh membawa mobil sendirian.
english: I can already drive, but I'm not allowed to take the car out alone.
tip: Bisa = able (skill), boleh = allowed (permission): bisa menyetir tapi belum boleh.

target: Boleh saya pinjam tangga kamu untuk mengganti lampu teras?
english: May I borrow your ladder to change the porch light?
tip: Boleh saya...? = May I...? — the everyday way to ask permission: Boleh saya pinjam...?
